title: How Blest the Sacred Tie That Binds
description: How Blest the Sacred Tie That Binds in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anna Laetitia Barbauld wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 397 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christian Friendship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How blest the sa-cred tie that binds In u-nion sweet ac-cord-ing minds! How swift the heav-enly course they run, Whose hearts, and faith, and hopes are one!

lines: How blest the sacred tie that binds
How swift the heavenly course they run,
Whose hearts, and faith, and hopes are one!
To each the soul of each how dear!
What jealous love, what holy fear!
How doth the generous flame within
Refine from earth, and cleanse from sin!
For human guilt and mortal woe;
Together shall they seek the place
Where God reveals his awful face:
How high, how strong, their raptures swell
There's none but kindred souls can tell.

licence: Public domain: Anna Laetitia Barbauld died in 1825.
credits: Words by Anna Laetitia Barbauld (1743–1825), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
